title: Duplicate messages and idempotency
description: Learn how to handle duplicate messages in distributed systems through idempotency. Understand patterns for making operations safe to retry.

data.text: In distributed systems, message delivery is at-least-once, meaning duplicates are inevitable. Idempotency ensures that processing the same message multiple times produces the same result as processing it once.
Network failures and retries are the primary causes of duplicate messages.

items: Producer retries when acknowledgment is lost
Consumer crashes after receiving but before acknowledging
Network partitions cause message redelivery
Queue redelivery policies on timeout
Producer redrives messages from dead-letter queue

data.title: Assume Duplicates
data.text: Design your consumers assuming duplicates will occur. Don't try to prevent them—handle them safely through idempotency.
An operation is idempotent if applying it multiple times has the same effect as applying it once.

items: GET requests are idempotent—reading doesn't change state
PUT with same data is idempotent—result is the same
POST is typically not idempotent—creates new resources
DELETE is idempotent—deleting twice has same result
Mathematical: x = 5 is idempotent, x++ is not

data.text: Track processed message IDs to detect and skip duplicates.

items: Store message ID in a table before processing
Check table on each message—skip if exists
Use unique constraints for atomic deduplication
Add TTL for cleanup of old IDs
Simple but requires additional storage

data.text: Use database constraints to make updates idempotent.

items: INSERT with unique constraint—fails on duplicate
UPDATE with WHERE clause—only changes if condition met
Upsert operations—insert or update atomically
Use natural keys rather than auto-increment IDs
Leverage database-level idempotency

data.text: Design operations that are safe to repeat.

items: SET value = X rather than increment
Use absolute values rather than deltas
Check current state before applying changes
Make operations commutative when possible
Document idempotency guarantees

data.title: Example
data.text: Instead of "increment balance by 10", use "set balance to calculated new value". The first approach fails on duplicates, the second succeeds safely.

items.title: Database-Level
items.description: Use unique constraints, upserts, conditional updates. Best when you control the database schema and can design for idempotency.

items.title: Application-Level
items.description: Deduplication tables, state tracking, idempotent logic. More flexible but requires careful implementation and testing.

items.title: Message-Level
items.description: Deduplication IDs in message metadata. Works when the messaging system supports it (e.g., SQS deduplication ID).

items: Deduplication adds overhead to every operation
Storage and cleanup of deduplication data
Complexity in business logic
May impact performance due to additional checks
Necessary for reliability in distributed systems

data.title: Don't Skip It
data.text: The cost of not handling duplicates is data corruption and bugs that are extremely hard to debug. Idempotency is worth the complexity.
